title: Extension and uniqueness of rigidified lines over a regular base
statement: Let $S$ be a regular locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], where regular means that every local ring is a regular local ring (its maximal ideal has a minimal generating set of cardinality its Krull dimension). Let $j:V\hookrightarrow S$ be a dense open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $p:G\to S$ be a separated smooth commutative group algebraic space of finite presentation [def-trf-algebraic-space], with geometrically integral fibres (each fibre after an algebraically closed field extension is reduced and irreducible); a commutative group algebraic space has multiplication, inverse and identity maps satisfying the group identities and commutativity. The identity is $e:S\to G$. Smoothness and finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. A rigidified line module is a line module $L$ on the small etale site of $G$ together with an isomorphism $e^*L\simeq\mathcal O_S$; its morphisms are line-module isomorphisms respecting that rigidification. Restriction induces an equivalence between the groupoid of rigidified line modules on $G$ and that on $G_V$. In particular every rigidified line on $G_V$ extends, and a specified rigidification-preserving isomorphism between restrictions of two extensions extends uniquely to an isomorphism on $G$. Pullback of these extensions and isomorphisms along any etale map $S'\to S$ is compatible with this restriction equivalence. For arbitrary maps of spaces, module pullback means tensor inverse image along their ringed etale sites [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model].

proof.text: First work over an affine open of $S$, hence with $S$ Noetherian and separated. The identity section makes all fibres nonempty. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-integral-fibre-vertical-divisors] to $p:G\to S$: $G$ is regular Noetherian and separated, and $G_V$ is dense. Thus the divisor-line dictionary [lem-sfb-regular-space-divisor-line-dictionary] applies both to $G$ and to its open $G_V$. We prove essential surjectivity and full faithfulness over such affine bases first, and glue over general $S$ in Step 6.

proof.text: Let $(L,\rho:e_V^*L\simeq\mathcal O_V)$ be given. Choose a nonzero rational section of $L$ on $G_V$ using [lem-sfb-regular-space-divisor-line-dictionary], with divisor $D_V=\sum n_i[Z_i]$. Take the closures $\overline Z_i$ in $G$ with reduced structure. Their generic points have the same local rings as in the open, so they still have codimension one. The finite sum $D=\sum n_i[\overline Z_i]$ is a Weil divisor of $G$. By the dictionary it gives a line $H=\mathcal O_G(D)$ and an isomorphism $\alpha:H|_{G_V}\simeq L$. Indeed $D|_{G_V}=D_V$, and the two rationally trivialized lines are identified by the unique isomorphism in that statement. This extends the unrigidified line without assuming $G$ is a scheme.

proof.text: Put $A=e^*H$ and $M=H\otimes p^*(A^\vee)$. Since $pe=1_S$, evaluation gives a canonical rigidification $e^*M=A\otimes A^\vee\simeq\mathcal O_S$. On $V$, put $t=\rho\circ e_V^*\alpha:A|_V\simeq\mathcal O_V$. Identify $M|_{G_V}$ with $L$ by the formula $h\otimes\lambda\mapsto\lambda(t^{-1}(1))\alpha(h)$. In local rank-one generators this is an invertible scalar times $\alpha$; on the identity section its composite with $\rho$ is exactly evaluation. Hence it preserves the specified rigidification, rather than merely its isomorphism class. Pullback and composition are interpreted using [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model].

proof.text: For full faithfulness let $(M_1,\rho_1)$ and $(M_2,\rho_2)$ be rigidified lines on $G$, and let $u_V:M_1|_{G_V}\simeq M_2|_{G_V}$ preserve their rigidifications. It gives an everywhere generating section on $G_V$ of $N=M_1^\vee\otimes M_2$, hence a nonzero rational section $s$ of $N$ on $G$. By [lem-sfb-regular-space-divisor-line-dictionary] its divisor $E$ is supported outside $G_V$. By [lem-sfb-smooth-integral-fibre-vertical-divisors] there is a unique divisor $D$ of $S$ supported outside $V$ with $E=p^*D$. The dictionary identifies the pair $(N,s)$ with $(\mathcal O_G(p^*D),s_{p^*D})$.

proof.text: The Cartier-line construction in [lem-sfb-regular-space-divisor-line-dictionary] has the explicit local form $\mathcal O(D)=f^{-1}\mathcal O$ when $f$ is a local rational equation for $D$, with canonical rational section $1$. By the flat-pullback clause of that statement, applied to the flat map $p$ between the regular Noetherian separated spaces $G$ and $S$ of Step 1, this identifies $(\mathcal O_G(p^*D),s_{p^*D})$ with $p^*(\mathcal O_S(D),s_D)$. Pull back this pair along $e$. Its rational section is defined at all generic points of $S$, because $s$ is defined on $G_V$ and every generic point of $S$ belongs to $V$. The induced rigidification of $e^*N$ identifies that rational section with $1$: this is exactly $\rho_2u_V=\rho_1$ on $V$. Its divisor on $S$ is consequently zero, while the displayed pullback and $pe=1$ identify that divisor with $D$. Thus $D=0$ and $E=0$. The dictionary now extends $s$ to a global generating section, giving $u:M_1\simeq M_2$. It preserves the rigidifications since their two regular maps agree on dense $V$. Any two extensions agree on dense $G_V$, hence are equal by the dictionary. This proves the required bijection on isomorphisms.

proof.text: For arbitrary locally Noetherian $S$, cover it by affine opens $S_i$. Steps 1--3 give extensions over each $G_{S_i}$. On each affine open contained in $S_i\cap S_j$, Steps 4--5 extend the prescribed comparison of their restrictions uniquely. Those maps agree on smaller affine opens by uniqueness, so glue to an overlap isomorphism. On triple intersections the two composites restrict to the same prescribed map over $V$; affine-local uniqueness makes them equal. The diagonal maps are identities for the same reason. Refine the cover of $G$ by the $G_{S_i}$ to a jointly surjective etale scheme family, as permitted by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Pull the lines and overlap maps to this family. They now satisfy exactly the scheme-atlas hypotheses of [lem-trf-algebraic-space-invertible-descent], which descends the line and its comparison with $L$. The identity rigidifications glue because the transitions preserve them. The Hom-bijection in the same descent statement glues the unique extensions of specified isomorphisms. Thus restriction is essentially surjective and fully faithful on the entire base, hence an equivalence of groupoids.

proof.text: Let $a:S'\to S$ be etale. By the etale clause of [lem-sfb-smooth-integral-fibre-vertical-divisors], $S'$ is again regular locally Noetherian, $V'=a^{-1}V$ is dense, and the pulled-back group has the required geometric properties. The group operations and identity pull back by the fibre-product identities. Composition compatibility in [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model] identifies restriction of a pulled-back line with pullback of its restriction, including the identity rigidification. Thus a pulled-back extension is an extension of the pulled-back given line. Its comparison with any extension constructed on $S'$ is the unique one supplied by full faithfulness already proved. The same uniqueness shows compatibility for specified isomorphisms and for successive etale maps: both composites restrict to the same map over the dense open. This is the asserted compatibility of equivalences. If $S$ is empty, every space and groupoid here is empty-base data with one line up to its unique isomorphism, and all arguments apply vacuously.
